source_text: I just hand an interesting idea, what if all the verbs that I have available via the C-c ; hydra became a set of tools that were available to Zaif agents?  That would make the AIF harness more concrete.  Another thing we could try to using our "aligned ledgers" between PBASE and R-numbers and intents is to try to understand how these "functions" (they aren't yet tools) sit inside the War Machine. For example, I hav three verbs classed as PERCEIVE ㊩ 🈖 ㊢ and the War Machine has three nodes in that layer, R19, R2, and R8.

reply_text:
Reading the R-node registry to line up the PERCEIVE marks with R19, R2, R8.㊥ (verbs as tools, and how they sit in the WM) The two ideas combine. If each C-c ; mark were a tool, a call could record the R-node it plays, the way the WM's `route-tag` records each of its own steps. On PERCEIVE, two of your three verbs match a WM node: ㊢ report is R2 (structured observation) and ㊩ report-problem is R8 (present-fit mismatch). 🈖 explain matches none of them. R19 has no counterpart among the marks. Its counterpart is 象 itself, which reads what you want from your text the way R19 reads a mission's preferences from its text. Shall I write this alignment out as a table for all 23 marks, before any tool work?

🈖 (why R19 pairs with 象 rather than a mark) R19 reads a mission's preferences (C) from the mission's own text when the click runs. Every quote is pinned to its span, and a typed absence is recorded when nothing is stated. 象 does the same thing to your turns: fragments with spans, each with an intent reading. So in an operator → agent flow, R19 is the agent reading your turn. In this layer, two of the three operations are things an agent says (㊢, ㊩) and one is how it reads you. 🈖 explain may belong in BELIEVE as a belief update (R3), or at R2 as an interpretation, since your D3 ruling makes interpretations observations entering at R2. I haven't settled that.

㊢ (the WM side already does part of this) `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/wm-click-acts.edn` tags each WM click act with a stage, an R-node and a `:nearest-intent`:
- select-policy (R6) is already tagged `:prioritize`, i.e. ㊝.
- construct-cascade (R13) is already tagged `:propose`, i.e. ㊭.
- In the ACT layer, dispatch-author is R16, which fits 🈸 ask-action, and verify-review is R9, which fits ㊬ verify.
- observe-world (R2) has `:nearest-intent :none`. By the reading above, it should be `:report` (㊢).

㊩ (an inconsistency) That same file tags request-interpretation as `:PERCEIVE :R7`, but `p4ng/empirics-futon/control-stages.edn` puts R7 in BELIEVE. One of the two files is wrong.

㭭 (Zai tools, concretely) There would be one tool per mark. Each takes a required target (the evidence id or paragraph it answers) and the text, and writes an act tagged with its intent, PBASE stage and R-node. That would give us:
- The bracketed target the proforma asks for becomes required, so no label arrives unconnected.
- The 🈸 tool posts its offer directly, so the parse-it-from-the-reply route I added today wouldn't be needed for these agents.
- An agent turn becomes a sequence of staged acts that the Agency skeleton and the Fong glue can check, for example an ACT with nothing in PERCEIVE upstream of it.

I haven't looked yet at how Zai agents are given tools today, so I can't say how much plumbing this needs.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I write the 23-mark × R-node table, with a confidence for each row and the WM act where one exists, next to `wm-click-acts.edn`? I'd start from PERCEIVE and leave the tools until after you've looked at it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the bell to codex-10) The bell is sent, and codex-10 is already working on it. It asks codex-10 to:
- **Write `futon2/holes/labs/A-self-heal.md`** from its own recent turns: run the WM in a debugger, dispatch a fix for each defect and have it reviewed, then stop and switch back on when a stated observation holds. It should describe what actually happened, citing the turns and commits.
- **Fill the slots of its cascade draft:** what kind of task this is, the next move, when to stop, which injured capability it repairs, and the countable condition for switching ordinary work back on, as WR-26 requires.
- **Optionally edit the cascade:** use this real injury in its injured example, and say what happens when no repair algorithm matches.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how to follow it)
- **Job:** `invoke-1790915880255-30166-6552bb4c`, which you can check at `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/<id>`.
- **Park:** `park-23f41841-d24a-4028-8a08-9bea495b8bde`, with a 45-minute deadline.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (codex-10's A-self-heal) codex-10's work checks out. `futon2/holes/labs/A-self-heal.md` (commit `8bb5b1880`) writes down the procedure it actually followed: debugger stop → one bounded repair → independent review → hot-load → explicit restart. It fills every slot of the cascade. The condition for switching ordinary work back on can be counted: one controlled click with all seven receipts present and none of five failure markers. The cascade's injured example now uses this real injury and selects `:run-self-heal` (futon3 `a044d286e`). One thing needs your decision. For "injured, no matching repair algorithm", codex-10 chose to abstain and keep ordinary work excluded. That contradicts your 2026-09-29 ruling that the WM must not abstain.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked)
- **Cited commits:** all ten futon2 commits the file cites as receipts exist, and their subjects match what it says they did, for example `7bc98c8ee` "Stop debugger on terminal selection abstention". The futon5a lifecycle fix it cites also exists.
- **The file is honest about its limits.** It says the receipts show where the procedure came from but don't meet the switch-back condition, because no repaired click has completed yet. It leaves time and token budgets as `:bind-at-launch` holes rather than inventing them. The cascade example binds 300000 ms / 10000 tokens, which is fine for a launch example.
- **The cascade EDN reads.** Each commit touches only its one file. The paused click wasn't touched.
- **The causal check is unchanged.** The real injury doesn't alter the structure, so the three cases come out as before. The difference is that the third case is now a declared, typed abstention rather than a gap.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the no-match case) codex-10's reasoning is sound as far as it goes: don't do M/E/T work while the click path is broken. But there's an alternative that keeps your ruling. When no repair algorithm matches, select the A item "write the missing repair algorithm from what was done". That's exactly what you asked me to bell codex-10 to do an hour ago, done by hand. Making it the no-match filler would mean the policy never abstains in that state: it either repairs, or writes down how to repair.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (one decision) Shall I ask codex-10 to replace the abstention with that "write the missing A item" filler?
